A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same L2-VMAS research. Their main text, equations, Tables 1-10, Figures 1-11, and Appendices A-D are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy and token-consumption experiments, memory ablations, sensitivity analyses, and generalization results in Sections 2 and 4 and Appendices B and D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The dual perception/thinking memories, compression and memory management, entropy-triggered retrieval and injection, and three-stage training recipe in Section 3 and Appendix C remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use GQA for main training and evaluate MMBench, MMStar, RealWorldQA, SimpleVQA, MuirBench, BLINK, MVBench, and LVBench. Table 10's cross-dataset generalization coverage is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same Single and/or VMAS comparators across backbones, model sizes, topologies, and datasets. The newly cited Yu et al. (2026) work is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Metrics, agent-turn evaluations, model configurations, and Table 4 settings match. Section 4.1 changes 'two-stage' to 'three-stage', resolving an inconsistency with v1's existing Section 3.4, Appendix C.5, and Table 4; it does not introduce a different training protocol.

E4.justification: Memory-specialization and triggering analyses, scalability experiments, component ablations, parameter sensitivities, and cross-dataset generalization studies are retained unchanged, including Figures 5-6 and 10-11 and Tables 6-10.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The entropy standard deviation used for memory triggering is an unchanged method component, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Result entries in Tables 1-3 and 5-10 and the plotted outcomes are unchanged. Both retain the reported 2.7-5.4% average accuracy improvements and 21.3-44.8% token reductions; the appendices add no new outcomes in v2.

T1.justification: Mathematical definitions and equations in Section 3 and Appendix C remain unchanged, including compression, chunking, memory retrieval, entropy, and gating formulations. The chunk-boundary equation moves between pages without a mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scaling-wall diagnosis and contributions concerning dual latent memory, proactive orchestration, and improved accuracy-cost scalability. No core scientific claim is added, removed, or strengthened.

C2.justification: Interpretations of memory specialization, scalability, and task-dependent benefits remain unchanged, including Appendix D.2's explanation of small performance losses. The added generic Impact Statement supplies no substantive new limitation or interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 removes the explicit code-repository link from v1's abstract without providing a replacement elsewhere. Section 4.1 also corrects the training-stage wording; the detailed training recipe, hardware, hyperparameters, and appendix prompt remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Yu et al. (2026), 'The latent space: Foundation, evolution, mechanism, ability, and outlook', citing it in Section 3.2 and Appendix A.2. The broader literature review and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds brief Impact Statement and Acknowledgment sections, updates the publication footnote, and corrects the training-stage wording. The main narrative and appendix organization are retained without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: There are limited changes to table sizing, spacing, and text placement, including Figure 6 preceding rather than following the scalability discussion in reading order. All figures, tables, captions, and underlying graphical content are retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting Section 4.1 improves consistency, but v1 already describes three-stage training in Section 3.4 and Appendix C.5. With methods and evidence unchanged, removing the sole code-repository pointer reduces implementation discoverability. This practical loss outweighs the limited editorial and citation gains.
